Q: AI/ML student with projects but weak fundamentals because of heavy LLM usage — how should I realistically improve for internships? A:

In a sane world, an intern doesn't need to know how to code larger things or even a small complete project, just given pieces, and to not make beginner mistakes. It's supposed to be a learning position, not an underpaid senior dev. DSA exercises (or other exercises) are there to show ability to reason and to solve said pieces of larger problems.

We do not live in a perfectly sane world.

It turns out demands during interviews even for entry-level positions blow up -> people learn how to pass an interview rather than how to be good developers. Theory or DSA coding comes up approximately never in real work because using an existing implementation (library) is easier and usually good enough. Nobody cares if you used AI and sometimes it's encouraged since time is money. What you should focus on depends on if you want to pass interviews or actually be a productive worker... if it's the latter, communication to make sure you're on the right track, general problem solving, keeping up to date with latest developments in the topics you're focusing on (once you've found such a topic).

Q: What are the best practices for Common Lisp/SBCL via Docker, especially with multithreading? A:

Indirect answer: there are Docker images out there that do install Quicklisp (or use Roswell, or install qlot, or ocicl). Did you found them for inspiration? https://github.com/CodyReichert/awesome-cl/#docker-images

I'm used to manipulating images and binaries with Hunchentoot (except not in Docker). As with any other multithreaded program, you can't "save lisp and die" from a running image and expect it saves everything, including the threads. No, you build a binary, define an entry point, and start the web server in the main function. Classical, simple. Then it works.

NB: depends on how you run your program, but you may have to make the main thread busy (or the web server thread on the foreground), so that your lisp doesn't immediately exits after startup. Example: https://lispcookbook.github.io/cl-cookbook/scripting.html#for-web-apps (using sleep).

my 2c.

Q: Unable to load shared library 'kernel32.dll' or one of its dependencies A:

Check if dotnet/dotnet-docker issue 618, which does report a similar error message could help.

Make sure you install it in your runtime and not in your dotnet build.

Moving the install up to under FROM microsoft/dotnet:2.2-aspnetcore-runtime AS base solved my issue

Q: What service is behind the referrer "android.clients.google.com"? A:

BLOCK IT ⚠️

If you're not using any API connected to Google or Firebase, block it

In our case, we got hacked by actors who used zero touch enterprise enrolment (MDM) and this endpoint was used to modify, push again, or delete any data on compromised devices

When sinking the endpoint domain and or IP, we noticed some positive changes. Rule of thumb, if you don't know, block it. Better be too strict than not enough

TLDR : Block it if not recognised, it can be used against you
